cards.headline: Four taken to hospital after fire breaks out in Choa Chu Kang flat
bullets: Four people were hospitalised after a fire in a Choa Chu Kang HDB flat on May 31.
The fire started in the living room of a 14th-floor unit and caused significant smoke damage.
Firefighters put out the blaze with water jets.
The cause of the fire is currently being investigated.

cards.headline: Defence spending alone may not translate into better capabilities, says Chan Chun Sing
bullets: Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing says how money is spent matters more than how much is spent.
He noted that high defence spending does not always lead to better capabilities.
Chan stressed the importance of reassuring other countries as defence spending increases.
Singapore and 16 other countries launched a framework to protect underwater infrastructure.

cards.headline: Every three steps, one bow: More than 7,000 devotees perform Buddhist ceremony to mark Vesak Day
bullets: Over 7,000 Buddhists did a ritual with bows every three steps for Vesak Day.
The ceremony took place at Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery.
Participants walked a route that was shorter this year due to construction.
The ritual aims to purify minds and atone for past wrongdoings.

cards.headline: With 10 weeks left to the PSLE English oral, use revision strategies that will make a difference
bullets: PSLE English and mother tongue oral exams start August 12.
AI tools can help your child practise for the English oral exam.
A free trial offers practice reading and conversation topics.
Experts suggest focusing on revision strategies, not just cramming.
Parents should build confidence and avoid dwelling on past test results.

cards.headline: Chan Chun Sing calls for more partnerships with like-minded countries as nature of conflicts evolves
bullets: Singapore led a 17-country effort to protect vital underwater cables.
Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing wants more flexible partnerships with other countries.
He said countries need to work together on new issues like military AI.
Singapore also launched a centre to counter cyber threats in ASEAN.

cards.headline: Shangri-La Dialogue helps countries reduce the chances of misunderstanding, miscalcuation: Chan Chun Sing
bullets: The Shangri-La Dialogue helps countries avoid misunderstandings and mistakes.
A new framework to protect underwater cables was launched by 17 countries.
Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing urged respect for China's participation level.
Countries need to reassure others of their intentions, not just spend more on defence.

cards.headline: Watch: Singapore Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing speaks at Shangri-La Dialogue on security partnerships
bullets: Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing spoke at the Shangri-La Dialogue on security.
He said conflicts now affect many places, not just one area.
Disruptions in one region can impact global supply chains everywhere.
Chan stressed the importance of maritime rights for all countries.
The dialogue is Asia's main defence and security meeting.

cards.headline: ASEAN set to sign landmark regional digital economy framework agreement in  November 2026
bullets: ASEAN countries will sign a new digital economy deal in November 2026.
This agreement aims to make digital trade easier and safer across Southeast Asia.
It will help businesses and consumers connect and transact more confidently online.
The deal covers new areas like AI, fintech, and source code protection.

cards.headline: Does a restaurant need to go viral to survive? Red House Seafood’s Christopher Chang hopes not
bullets: Red House Seafood is celebrating 50 years in business.
Owner Christopher Chang avoids social media to stay true to the restaurant's values.
He believes in genuine hard work over chasing viral trends.
The restaurant started the trend of eating fried mantou with chilli crab.
Red House Seafood also created the popular dish 'pao fan'.

cards.headline: Not just checking a box: How Buddhist teachings inspire these two men to give blood regularly
bullets: Two Buddhist men donate blood regularly, seeing it as living out compassion and generosity.
Jereme Wong, 50, has donated blood for two decades, viewing it as an 'other-centred' act.
Macs Chen, 34, donates blood every three months, seeing it as contributing to society.
Both men integrate Buddhist teachings of kindness and generosity into their blood donation practice.

cards.headline: Faith in Luis Enrique leads PSG to back-to-back Champions League titles
bullets: PSG won the Champions League for the second year in a row.
They beat Arsenal in the final after a 1-1 draw and penalties.
Coach Luis Enrique built the team on trust and playing together.
Players say he is more of a leader than just a coach.
The team is already aiming to win it a third time.

cards.headline: Domestic capital reshapes China real estate deals as asset managers redirect to ‘China-for-China’ play
bullets: Singapore firms like Mapletree and CapitaLand are looking to Chinese money for property deals.
They are setting up funds in Chinese currency to invest only in China.
This is happening because foreign investors are avoiding China's property market.
Chinese insurers and wealthy individuals are now funding these deals.

cards.headline: Georgia uncorks the value of Stalin’s 40,000-bottle wine collection
bullets: Georgia will auction about 40,000 bottles of wine once owned by Stalin.
The collection includes rare French and Georgian wines, some dating back to the 1800s.
Funds from the sale will be used to start a wine education school in Georgia.
Georgia claims to be the birthplace of wine, with an 8,000-year winemaking history.

cards.headline: Shanda co-founder sells Tanglin Hill bungalow for S$76 million
bullets: A Tanglin Hill bungalow sold for S$76 million.
The seller is Chrissy Luo, co-founder of Shanda Group.
She bought the property in 2011 for S$38.8 million.
The buyer is a Singapore citizen buying for a minor.
The bungalow is in a Good Class Bungalow Area.

cards.headline: In World Cup swansong, Argentina’s Messi to go full throttle to retain crown
bullets: Argentina aims to defend their World Cup title in Lionel Messi's final tournament.
Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo also seeks a strong World Cup finish.
Austria returns to the World Cup after a 28-year absence.
England had a perfect qualifying campaign, scoring 22 goals without conceding.
Debutants Jordan are unlikely to advance past the group stage.

cards.headline: 6 tourists injured after tour bus overturns on Genting Highlands road following 3-vehicle collision
bullets: Six tourists were hurt when a tour bus overturned after a three-vehicle crash on a Genting Highlands road.
The bus driver, aged 55, was arrested for suspected reckless driving.
The first bus reportedly lost control on a bend, hitting an SUV and then another bus.
The injured were treated at the scene before being sent to hospital.

cards.headline: 2 including boy, 8, taken to hospital after accident involving 5 cars & motorcycle on PIE towards Tuas
bullets: A total of five cars and one motorcycle crashed on the PIE towards Tuas.
Two people, including an 8-year-old boy, were sent to the hospital.
The accident happened on May 30 morning near the Adam Road exit.
Traffic was blocked in the right lanes of the expressway.

cards.headline: 'Isn't it strange?': Japan defence minister addresses 'new militarism' accusations, compares with China at 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue
bullets: Japan's Defence Minister says Japan has no nuclear weapons, unlike some countries, yet is called militaristic.
He spoke at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, noting Japan's history as a peace-loving nation.
Japan wants open dialogue with China, but their Defence Minister did not attend the summit.
Concerns were raised about Japan's historical apologies and China's military growth.
Japan's defence policy is not aimed at any specific country, he stated.

cards.headline: Catch Jumptopia Inflatables, Member Deals & Flight Giveaways At Frasers Property Singapore Malls This June Hols
bullets: Four different inflatable playgrounds are available at Frasers Property Singapore malls this June.
Kids can try Kiztopia Mission: Ninja Trials obstacle course at The Centrepoint from June 1st to 14th.
Spend $150 to get bonus FRx points or a $15 gift card with a Citi Mastercard.
Shop on Fridays for half-price electronics and 1-for-1 meal deals on the FRx app.
Spend $50 for a chance to win flights to Vancouver or 1 million FRx points.
